chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

He was asked, "Can the Imamate be in a paternal uncle or a maternal uncle?" So he عليه السلام said, "No." I said, "Then in a brother?" He عليه السلام said, "No." I said, "Then in whom?" He عليه السلام said, "In my son." And at that time, he عليه السلام had no son.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: the divinely ordained leadership of the Imam
key_terms.لَا: a negation used here to deny those lines of succession
key_terms.وَلَدِي: my son; indicating descent through offspring

ai.seo_question: Does the Imamate return to a brother or extend to an uncle in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imamate does not pass to a paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or brother, but continues in the Imam's descendants. It highlights the designated continuity of the Imamate through the offspring of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, even before a son had been born to him عليه السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>,

having been asked, ‘Can the Imamate happen to be in a paternal uncle or a maternal uncle?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. So I said, ‘So, (can it be) in a brother?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So in whom (would it be)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’. And he<sup>asws</sup> was such that in those days, there was no son for him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ who has said the following. “Abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) was once asked, “Can Imamat continue in uncles?” He replied, “No, it can not happen.”

The narrator has said that he asked the Imams (a.s.), “Can it continue in a brother?” He replied, “No, it can not happen.” I then asked, “With who then it can continues?” He replied, “It will continue with my children.” In those days he hadd no children.”
